"Respected Father Bishoy,
I just wanted to share a few reflections regarding the idea raised by some that the Orthodox Church is the 'only right' church. While it is wonderful for anyone to cherish the history and deep traditions of their own church, claiming that only one denomination possesses the truth is incredibly divisive—and it completely contradicts the true essence of Christ’s message.
Honestly, if what people are learning from their church is that other Christians are 'wrong' or lesser than them, then they are missing the most critical part of the faith. Jesus did not establish a monopoly for a single institutional structure; He built a global community of believers. He explicitly said in John 13:35: 'By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another'—He did not say people would know us by our denominational labels.
Therefore, I respectfully ask that you try to change this mindset and perspective. If you are unable to change this outlook, then we ask that you at least follow the clear words and teachings of Jesus Christ.
There are many other Christian traditions that focus deeply on God’s word, equality, and living in the spirit of the early New Testament church. Their faith is just as real, authentic, and deeply rooted. Acting as if one church is spiritually superior to everyone else does not show strength of faith—it only shows a lack of humility. True spiritual maturity lies in recognizing God’s work in the lives of all believers, not in looking down on others just to feel right."

Having breakfast on the ornately painted rooftop terrace with the view of the Valley of the Kings was truly memorable. The hotel is quaintly decorated and the rooms are spacious & cozy, made us feel at home.

The location of the hotel is quiet but strategic enough - it is walking distance to the ferry & restaurants - we had interesting sights along the way (dry cleaning, essential oils shop, mixed nuts shop, mini marts, tuk-tuks, camels, horses, donkeys). It is also close to the hot air balloon launch site, so we did not have to wake up too early for our sunrise hot air balloon ride.

The staff were warm & welcoming, especially the famous Mahmoud, he was the receptionist, the chef & the waiter - all in one. We had our luggages brought up & down during check-in & check-out, which was nice.

After check-out, we left Luxor to go to Aswan. When we reached Aswan, one of my family members just realised that he left his green jacket in his room at Cleopatra Hotel Luxor. I immediately asked the hotel to look for it and they found it! Then I asked our lovely tour guide in Luxor, Maria, to help us - she waited at the ferry dock and the hotel staff came to meet her at the ferry dock to pass her the jacket. Maria then had the jacket delivered to us in Aswan. We were so grateful how helpful & sincere our tour guide and the hotel staff were, thank you so much!

The cleanliness of the bedroom & bathroom could be improved a bit. The floor was dusty & the fridge seemed like it has not been used in a long time, it was unplugged when we checked in, so when we opened it, the smell coming from it was not so fresh.

Some of the lights on the bedroom wall did not work. The light bulbs in the bedroom & bathroom were a mix of cool white & warm white. It would be nicer if all the light bulbs were warm white for extra coziness.

A hand bidet would be better than the built-in bidet.

The breakfast was delicious but it would be nice to have some simple fruits & vegetables like bananas, tomatoes & cucumbers too.

We (a young german couple) stayed at the Happy Land Hotel for about a week in March 2026 and had a wounderful stay.
Our room 121 had a double bed and private bathroom. It was clean, the facilities worked to our satisfaction and for warm water no long waiting was needed. There was no wardrobe but a chair and a nightstand. The windows could be shut completely, just  blinds or an insect screen.
Our highlight in terms of the hotel itself definitely was the rooftop which you get free unlimited access to. We had chill evenings in cozy lighting. There you can also meet other guests - it honestly feelt like a livingroom.
While the room was great, the staff and food was the true highlight of our stay.
It started off with us being able to check-in in the middle of the night (due to our flight) and the iconic car of our hotel-organised taxi pick up. We recommend you to never miss the breakfast from 7am-10am (unlike we did our first morning) because with it you'll get just the right start of the day. During our stay the buffet usually consisted of fluffy pita-bread(?), cucumber, tomato, a feta-like cheese that melts in your mouth, some kind of cooked eggplant-tomato-mix, potatos and a dip made of beans. Also be prepared to be offered an omelette by the cook. He is one of few staff members that doesn't really speak English but in the evening (roughly after 8pm) you shouldn't hesitate to ask him for a meal. The Menu is displayed at nearly every table. In addition you can get free tea and coffe at nearly every time on the rooftop.
The taxi pick-up and meals are paid at checkout - we paid less than 6 EUR for 2 persons per evening-meal.
In conclusion we were very happy guest at Happy Land Hotel and would definitely recommend to stay here!

The list goes on for its negatives but include the following:

Multiple shower issues in multiple rooms including no hot water, terrible shower pressure and awkward shower position.

One working plug in the room which was located between our heads. This was due to the hotel having no queen beds so it was two singles shoved together, hence the plug in between us.

The hallways were a mess: sometimes no lights were on making it very dark, housekeeping equipment was constantly left lying around, including pita breads lying amongst the clean towels and sheets…

Unhelpful and unfriendly staff, barring one nice gentleman who looks like Fred Vasseur and a kind housekeeping lady. Front desk couldn’t care less about our issues and did very little to fix them or apologise.

On many occasions, the staff got our food and drinks orders wrong and made it difficult to change the bills. Also the service is EXTREMELY slow.

The place in general is very dated and don’t even think about using the wifi. It does not work.

Further to the lack of queen beds: The way they connect the two single beds is to use sheets that are too small to go all the way around the beds so they come loose in the night.

The elevator is also a nightmare: limited to three people at a time, confusing buttons and always drops about 20 cm as it comes to a stop making you think you’re about to plummet down.

To summarise, the hotel is shoddy and uncomfortable, the staff are unhelpful and unfriendly, and you can definitely find better value for money elsewhere.

We arrived exhausted after driving seven hours, only to be given a room with extremely uncomfortable single beds. We were unable to sleep at all and had to request a room change on the first night, which added to our exhaustion and frustration.
When we later asked to extend our stay by two nights, staff told us the hotel was fully booked. However, we immediately checked Booking.com and saw multiple rooms still available (king, queen, and twin). This lack of transparency was concerning.
We experienced multiple issues with billing and staff conduct. Despite authorising the hotel to charge our card for purchases, staff escalated a minor issue unnecessarily and handled it in a very intimidating manner. We were even told we would be charged USD 120 for alcohol that was already opened and clearly ours, which felt completely inappropriate.
One of the most upsetting incidents was when a male staff member attempted to enter our room, knocking only once and opening the door without waiting for permission, while I was not clothed. This was extremely uncomfortable and a serious breach of privacy.
The service overall was poor, and the prices were extortionate. A standard cocktail cost around £32 GBP, which is excessive even by luxury hotel standards. The BBQ meal was also disappointing, and although we raised concerns with restaurant staff, nothing was resolved.
Parking was another major issue. There was no valet available during our stay, despite this being implied. The car park is actually behind the hotel, not in front as one would reasonably expect, and this was not mentioned on Booking.com, causing confusion and inconvenience.
Several interactions with staff made us feel that tourists are treated as easy targets rather than valued guests.
This hotel trades heavily on its historic name, but the reality is poor service, uncomfortable rooms, excessive pricing, and serious lapses in professionalism and guest safety. We would not return and would strongly caution others to think twice before booking.

Location & Accessibility

Perfect for Sightseeing: The location is excellent. You can easily walk to Luxor Temple and the Ferry Crossing to the West Bank.

Easy Transport: It’s a quick taxi or horse carriage ride to Karnak Temple, making early morning visits very convenient.

Property Highlights & Views

Rooftop Terrace: The absolute highlight of this property. You get amazing panoramic views of the Luxor Temple and the Valley of the Kings in the distance.

Staff: The staff were very courteous and helpful; they are clearly doing their best with the resources they have.

Room Quality & Dining

Cleanliness: The rooms are unfortunately not very clean, and the carpets, in particular, were quite dirty. As the saying goes, "you get what you pay for."

Breakfast: I found the breakfast quality to be disappointing and ended up eating elsewhere for the remainder of my stay.

Final Recommendation

Advice to Travelers: If you want to stay in this exact area but prefer higher cleanliness standards, I would recommend checking out the Nefertiti Hotel Luxor nearby.

Note to Management: The staff is great, but the property itself is in desperate need of an upgrade and better maintenance.

I sincerely warn all travelers coming to Luxor to stay far away from Amen Hotel. This is by far the worst hotel I have ever stayed in.

The air conditioner in the room is extremely noisy, roaring like an engine all night long. It was impossible to get any proper sleep and completely ruined my rest during the trip.

Worse still, the room was missing almost all basic amenities: no shampoo, no body wash, no toothbrushes or toothpaste, no disposable slippers, not even a drinking cup. The hotel lacks the most essential facilities for a basic stay, causing huge inconvenience throughout my visit.

The most outrageous part was the unreasonable extra charges at check-out. They charged me 25 yuan for just one bottle of plain water placed in the room, and the staff even asked for tips compulsively. Hidden fees and forced tipping are common here, plus their service attitude is rude and awful.

Poor hygiene, missing amenities, loud noise, terrible service, and random overcharging — this hotel has every single downside. Zero value for money and purely a trap for tourists. Please avoid this hotel at all costs!

My room came equipped with a kettle, coffee, tea and a full size refrigerator. There are ceiling fans, air-con and a space heater so anybody can make the temperature perfect for their needs. There is plenty of hot water and it has the fastest wifi of any hotel I’ve stayed in, in Egypt, so this is a perfect location for digital nomads or more budget conscious travelers who can utilize the kitchen facilities. There’s a rooftop with stellar views, for viewing the sunrise hot air balloons or the evening sunset over the temples. I think my favorite thing about this place besides the pool are the owners. They are on property for anything you need, are so accommodating, quick for recommendations or a cup of tea AND have excellent English which is wonderful for those of us who don’t speak Arabic. I loved sitting in the courtyard, with a cup of tea, editing my photos from the day and listening to the call to prayer. This is a wonderful, inviting, peaceful spot for anyone’s trip to Luxor.

Last October 26,2025 my friends and I went to this Temple Complex as part of our trip to Egypt. We're cruising the Nile River and made a tour to Dendra.
Our guide Mohamed Ali introduced us to this magnificent historical site.
He is a great expert in Egyptian history, so he gave us a vast explanation of the Temple, both its exterior facade and the magnificent interior.
He told us that Hathor Temple is one of the best-preserved in ancient Egyptian sites. The temple was dedicated to Hathor one of the important and popular deities in ancient Egypt. She was associated with music, joy, dance and motherhood; she was also known as the lady of the sky.
Both, outside and inside of the Temple are impressed, the outer vestibule hall have 24 columns topped by four-sided capitals with the face of the goddess. The rear outer wall holds famous reliefs of Queen Cleopatra VII and her son Caesarion. Also, two large lion-headed waterspouts are located on the roof, and was used to drain water.
Inside the temple, Mohamed Ali explained us that the main hall contains 18 columns, and 6 additional columns in the second hall, that were designed to represent sistrums (musical instruments associated with Hathor).
Also,the ceilings were restored to show vivid, colorful scenes of the sky goddess Nut, zodiac signs, and astronomical charts, contrasting with areas still blackened by centuries of soot.
Then we walked through the sanctuary and chambers that
housed the statue of Hathor.
He told us about hidden crypto and roof staircase. We climbed up to the stone, spiraling staircase that allows access to the roof. There are small chapels dedicated to the union of Hathor and Horus are located.

Temple of Khnum:
The Temple of Khnum also known as the Temple of Esna, is a remarkably preserved ancient Egyptian sanctuary located on the west bank of the Nile River in the city of Esna, about 55 kilometers south of Luxor.
Dedicated primarily to Khnum, the ram-headed creator god believed to have fashioned mankind out of Nile clay on a potter's wheel. It also honors his consorts and the goddess Neith. The hall features 24 towering sandstone pillars. Every single column features a completely unique floral capital (palm leaves, lotus buds, papyrus fans, and Roman grapes), meaning no two columns are alike. While early foundations date back to the 18th Dynasty under Thutmose III, the visible structure was built during the Ptolemaic Period and heavily expanded under Roman rule (between 180 BC and 250 AD). The fully intact roof preserves vivid, colorful astronomical reliefs representing the sky goddess Nut, constellations, and a complete Roman-era zodiac calendar.
The Hypostyle Hall is the only fully excavated section surviving today. The rest of the vast temple complex remains buried underneath the modern town's residential houses.

When I walked into the restaurant, the waiter told me that I had to wait until after 1 PM to order the main course, as they were only serving desserts and drinks at that time. I completely understood and accepted that.

While I was waiting for 1 PM, a couple in front of me ordered a pizza. The waiter informed them that the pizza would take 25 minutes to prepare and asked if that was okay. They agreed.

At 1 PM, I ordered the main course called “Grill Mix” (see attached photos). The waiter did not inform me how long it would take, so I just placed the order and waited.

After 40 minutes, my food still hadn’t arrived. Meanwhile, other customers around me — even those who ordered later than I did — had already received and finished their meals. I asked the waitress whether my food was still being prepared. She simply said, “Just wait, it’s on the way.”

Another 20 minutes later (a total of one hour), my food finally arrived (see attached photos). I immediately told them I thought there must be a mistake because the dish looked completely different from the menu photo. I asked if it had been delivered incorrectly.

The staff member who helped me order said, with a bad attitude and an unfriendly expression, “Yes, this is your order.”

I was shocked. The dish looked totally different from the picture. I tasted it and found that both the rice and grilled meat were cold — not even warm. I waited for one full hour and received food in that condition. And the meal cost $1200??? Honestly, it’s unbelievable.

When I finished eating and wanted to pay, I told the waitress I was ready to check out. She replied, “Just wait,” and continued cleaning tables. I felt extremely uncomfortable.

I can’t help but wonder if I was treated differently because I was dining alone, because I am Asian, or because I look young. I kept being told to “wait” while other customers were served promptly.

This was truly the worst experience I’ve ever had. If you don’t care about food quality, service attitude, or price, and you don’t mind being treated poorly, then maybe this place is for you.

Staying at this vintage hotel was an unforgettable experience, blending timeless charm with modern comfort in the most delightful way. From the moment I arrived, I was welcomed by the warm and attentive staff, who made every effort to ensure that my stay was smooth, comfortable, and truly memorable. Their professionalism was matched by a genuine sense of hospitality, which gave the entire place a homely yet elegant feel.
The hotel itself carries a unique character, with beautifully preserved vintage architecture and décor that transport you to another era while still offering all the conveniences of today. My room was exceptionally spacious, tastefully furnished, and offered a sense of calm and comfort. What stood out most, however, was the breathtaking view from the window—waking up each morning to such a stunning backdrop was an experience on its own.
Equally impressive was the hotel’s restaurant, which deserves special recognition. It is not just a place to eat, but an experience to savor. The menu was carefully curated, offering a wide selection of both local and international dishes, each prepared with great attention to detail and freshness. Every meal I had there was a highlight, from the flavorful breakfast to the exquisite dinner. And the view from the restaurant only elevated the entire dining experience—whether it was enjoying a morning coffee bathed in golden sunlight or a candlelit dinner overlooking the serene landscape.
The rooftop area was another favorite spot, perfect for unwinding in the evening while taking in panoramic views. Although some road noise could be heard at times, it was a small detail compared to everything else the hotel offered.
Overall, this vintage hotel and its exceptional restaurant create the perfect destination for anyone seeking relaxation, charm, and beauty in one place.

Our stay at Eden on the Nile in Luxor was truly magical from beginning to end. We arrived late in the evening, but the owners were completely prepared for us and stayed in touch throughout via WhatsApp, making everything feel easy and welcoming from the moment we landed.

Every morning we woke up to the most beautiful breeze coming off the Nile, surrounded by mango trees and stunning views along the riverbank. Breakfast was fresh and delicious every day — made-to-order omelettes, salad, yogurt, cheese, fresh bread, excellent coffee, and the most amazing black tea with freshly picked mint, which quickly became my favourite part of the morning.

What made this place especially unforgettable though was the warmth and atmosphere created by the owners and their wonderful family of cats and dogs. Honestly, they may have been the highlight of the entire trip — they made us feel completely at home and added so much comfort and happiness to our stay.

The owners also went above and beyond helping organise taxis and trusted drivers so we could easily explore the Valley of the Kings, Karnak Temple, and Luxor Temple without any stress.

Everything about Eden on the Nile felt peaceful, authentic, and special. I am so glad we chose to stay here and would recommend it to anyone visiting Luxor looking for somewhere beautiful, welcoming, and memorable.

"The Canary Pharaoh: A Journey That Touched the Soul"
They say Egypt isn't visited, it's felt. But what we never imagined was that this feeling would be so profound, so magical, and so transformative, thanks to our guide, affectionately known as the Canary Pharaoh, who united the group in his own unique way.

From the very first moment, we knew we were in the hands of someone special. Not only because of his vast knowledge of the ancient history of this sacred land, but also because of the passion with which he shared it with us. Every word he uttered had soul. Every anecdote, every explanation in front of a temple, a pyramid, or a hidden corner of the Nile, made us feel as if we were traveling through time.

The Canary Pharaoh is not just a guide: he is a storyteller, a bridge between cultures, a passionate devotee of the Egyptian legacy who has made his vocation an unforgettable experience for those of us lucky enough to share the journey with him. He led us through Egypt as if it were a dream we never wanted to wake up from. He showed us not only what we see, but what we feel: the energy of Karnak, the sacred silence of the Valley of the Kings, the mystery of the desert, and the vibrant life of Cairo.

But what touched us most was his humanity. His warmth, his complete dedication, and his attention to every detail so that each of us would have a unique experience. He made us laugh, feel moved, learn, and above all, connect with something much bigger than ourselves.

Today, looking back, we don't just remember the monuments or the photos. We remember the voice of the Canary Island Pharaoh guiding us under the Egyptian sun, his eyes shining with enthusiasm, and that feeling of experiencing something unrepeatable.

Thank you for showing us Egypt not as tourists, but as dreamers.

Thank you for being so much more than a guide.

Eternally grateful,
Your Katakitos Travelers.

My husband and I booked a three-day private tour package, and from the very first moment it was clear that this would be an unforgettable experience.
Day 1 – Saqqara, Dahshur & Memphis
Our guide, Dr. Azmy Salama, and our driver, Ahmed (Ghazal), picked us up directly in front of our hotel, and our adventure began. Azmy guided us through the Saqqara necropolis with incredible knowledge and attention to detail, and he took us to the fascinating Serapeum. We then continued to Dahshur, where we explored the Red Pyramid and the Bent Pyramid together, followed by a visit to Memphis.
Already on the first day, we felt completely safe and well taken care of, which was extremely important to us as we do not know the local culture or language. Azmy helped us not only as a guide but also with practical matters that would have taken us much longer on our own, such as buying a SIM card and exchanging money. From day one, we had full trust in both Azmy and Ahmed.
Day 2 – Giza Pyramids & GEM
On the second day, we visited the Giza Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM). This day was especially memorable because it was my birthday. During a coffee break at a local café, Azmy and Ahmed surprised me with a birthday cake and singing — a truly beautiful and thoughtful gesture that made my birthday very special.
Azmy showed us everything in great detail, shared insights and stories we would never have known otherwise, and his guidance through the GEM was excellent and engaging.
Day 3 – Old Cairo, Coptic Cairo & Islamic Cairo
On the third day, we explored Old Cairo, Coptic Cairo, and Islamic Cairo with Azmy. It was another wonderful day filled with history, culture, and meaningful explanations that brought the city to life.
Overall, Dr. Azmy Salama is an outstanding guide — knowledgeable, patient, attentive, and genuinely caring. Together with Ahmed, we always felt safe, relaxed, and welcomed. Thanks to them, we truly fell in love with Cairo. We are leaving Egypt feeling that we have gained not just an amazing experience, but also two friends.
We are already certain that we will return to explore other incredible places such as Luxor, the Valley of the Kings, Abu Simbel, and more — and we would not do it with anyone else.
Highly recommended!

Thank you so much for making my first trip to Cairo so memorable. To see the pyramids in itself is so magical, but to have you take us back in time through your facts and stories makes it even better.

I recently celebrated my graduation at L'Uliveto, and it was truly an unforgettable experience from start to finish.

We were warmly welcomed with a complimentary starter—freshly baked bread paired with a deliciously creamy tuna spread. It was a delightful way to begin the meal and set the tone for what was to come.

For the main course, we ordered the penne arrabbiata with shrimp, and it was absolutely delicious. The pasta was cooked perfectly, and the slight kick of spice made every bite rich and flavorful.

But the real star of the evening was the Italian pizza. The dough was thin, crispy, and incredibly fresh. Since it was a special occasion, they went the extra mile and made us a pizza with two different halves: one side was truffle funghi, earthy and aromatic, and the other was pastrami with cream cheese, which was indulgent and perfectly balanced. They even surprised us with a live pizza show, which added a magical, luxurious touch to the night. It was such a beautiful gesture that made me feel truly celebrated.

For drinks, we tried three different mocktails
The Virgin Maimi was my absolute favorite—refreshing with the perfect hint of coconut.

The Egyptian Breeze was a bold and zesty choice, ideal for sour lovers, with a strong cinnamon note that stood out beautifully.

As someone who doesn’t usually enjoy hibiscus, I was pleasantly surprised by their hibiscus mocktail, it was flavorful and refreshing.

The atmosphere was simply lovely, with an elegant ambiance and a breathtaking view of the Nile that made the evening even more special. The entire staff was kind, welcoming, and attentive—especially Peter, who went above and beyond to ensure everything was perfect. He was professional, helpful, and added a personal touch to our experience.

In every way, L'Uliveto made my graduation celebration truly extraordinary. It felt warm, joyful, and full of little thoughtful surprises. I can’t recommend this place enough if you’re looking for great food, a beautiful setting, and a memorable experience. Thank you to everyone at L'Uliveto for making it a night I’ll never forget. 🌿✨🎓

When my mother was in her first year of secondary school, she learned about the ancient Egyptians. From that moment on, she wanted to see the pyramids and the mask of Tutankhamun.

In 2011, it was almost time, but halfway through their Nile cruise, a civil war broke out. My parents had seen everything except Cairo.

They looked online for trips to Egypt several times, but there was always some unrest. They also wanted to wait until the new Egyptian Museum was open. In early 2026, they decided to just go, and I went along with them as their daughter.

I had been following King Fisher online for years and knew that I wanted to travel with them if I ever went to Egypt. Their website contains a lot of advice and good tips, but what we particularly liked was that Miriam was always reachable via WhatsApp.

She put together the perfect trip for us: 3 full days in Cairo, including not only the Pyramids of Giza but also Shakkara. We also visited the new GEM and the old city with the Coptic quarter. All with a private guide and driver. One week before our departure, war broke out again in the Middle East. Egypt was safe, but did we dare take the risk? Miriam reassured us, and we left. And: she was right. Not for a single moment did we feel unsafe.

Our local guide Amira took perfect care of us, along with the various drivers. This allowed us to enjoy a wonderful trip without a care in the world. The schedule was flexible; we could have lunch at places I had chosen, and there was time to buy souvenirs.

With this trip, my mother's nearly 60-year-old bucket list dream came true: a visit to the pyramids and the mask of Tutankhamun. It was even more beautiful than in the stories told by her history teacher.

King Fisher, thank you for making this dream trip come true!

We had a very lovely stay at Zen Wellness Resort in Aswan. From the warm welcome to the farewell, the whole team was incredibly friendly and made us feel very comfortable throughout the stay.

I had high expectations when visiting the resort, as it is presented as a wellness resort where you can relax and enjoy a peaceful experience. Unfortunately, my experience was far from that.
We arrived early and ended up waiting well beyond the check-in time. We were asked to wait by the pool, but there weren’t enough seats for all the guests, so we had to sit in the sun. Ordering food was another challenge. Every time we tried to order something, we were told the kitchen was busy and were pushed to place all orders at once, regardless of when we actually wanted to eat. Even then, the food took a long time to arrive.

The food itself was not good. Whenever we gave feedback, we kept hearing the same response: that this is “healthy food.” Healthy food doesn’t mean it has to be tasteless. We ordered meat and fish but what we received was different from what was listed on the menu without any prior notice. When we asked, the response was simply that the available cut was different.. which is not acceptable and we should have been informed and given a choice. The same happened with the fish too!!!

We ended up bringing wood ourselves because we were cold. We also asked for dessert and no one followed up or even confirmed whether it was available.

The next morning, we had children with us and wanted to order their food first, then place the rest of the breakfast order later, we were told to order the entire order at once because “the chef prefers it that way” which was very inconvenient!!

Honestly, I couldn’t understand how the system works in this place whether there is any organization at all or if everything depends on individual mood!

There are various options available, and the staff are very friendly and helpful.

Confirmed options:
Boat tour: 1 hour, 1000 EGP (Felucca tour not available)
Taxi arrangement for next trip: 850 EGP
Free tuktuk to Nubian village: 08:00–23:30
Dinner last order: 21:30
Breakfast: 08:00–10:00
Airport transfer by taxi: 950 EGP
Pool: open 24 hours

The taxi arrangement felt relatively expensive, but if you’re not satisfied, you can take the free tuktuk to the village and try to negotiate with local taxis or tuktuks there on your own.

The Sacred Lake at Karnak has a calm, almost timeless atmosphere. Built during the reign of Thutmose III in the 18th Dynasty, it was used for purification rituals by priests before entering the temple. Standing by the water, you can imagine

This was a highly sacred pool (lake) used by ancient Egyptian priests to cleanse (purify) their bodies.

Measuring approximately 120 meters by 77 meters, it is the largest sacred pool remaining in Egypt.

Cleanliness was paramount in ancient Egyptian temples.

To avoid disrespecting the gods, priests who entered the innermost parts of the temple were obligated to cleanse themselves here daily.

The priests washed their entire bodies in the water of this sacred pool four times a day: twice during the day and twice at night.

Only priests who had completely shaved their hair and purified themselves in this pool were permitted to perform sacred rituals.

In ancient Egyptian festivals, special boats called "sacred boats" carrying statues of the gods were used.

Not only in large festivals that took place outside the temple, but also within this sacred pool, sacred rituals were performed at night, involving floating boats carrying gods (such as Amun, Mut, and Khonsu) and moving them across the water.

This pond is linked to the water level of the Nile River, and groundwater naturally springs up from it.

Therefore, even after more than 3,000 years, the water has never dried up and continues to be contained within it.

In ancient Egyptian mythology, it was believed that before the creation of the world, the universe was filled with chaotic, dark water called "Nun" (primordial water).

The sacred pond is a recreation of this "primordial water (Nun)," and the fact that the sun rises from here every day symbolizes the world being reborn (regenerated) anew every day.

I had a pleasant stay at Sweet Hostel in Luxor. The location is excellent—just a 2-minute walk from the train and bus stations, and about 5 minutes from Luxor Temple. It’s very central, and the room was reasonably quiet.
The building itself is quite old and there’s no elevator. The hostel also has another branch on the West Bank, and they can move your reservation there if availability allows.
Breakfast is served near the reception and includes omelette, cheese, marmalade, fava beans, banana and bread, and coffee or tea. It’s simple but enough to start your day well.
The beds are wide and comfortable, and the air conditioning works well. There’s also a ceiling fan, which is a nice addition.
On the downside, basic toiletries like toilet paper and shampoo are not provided automatically—you need to ask the staff for them. The Wi-Fi could also be improved.
One of the highlights of my stay was the owner’s help in organizing trips. They arranged a shared tour at a good price to the West Bank, including visits to Valley of the Kings and Temple of Hatshepsut, as well as a hot air balloon ride. This made my trip very efficient and enjoyable.

Originally we booked a different hotel on Booking, but on arrival it was really disappointing, the rooms were dark and humid, not at all in good condition. So we decided to walk around and look for another hotel and stumbled at Windsor

Windsor Hotel Luxor – Exceptional Hospitality, But Could Be Cleaner

British-Style Hospitality
This hotel operates on the principles of British hospitality, and it shows in the well-trained staff and high service standards—comparable to those of a UK 5-star hotel. Upon arrival, we were warmly greeted with a welcome drink, a non-alcoholic sweet cocktail.

Booking & Check-In
* The website allowed us to book a three-single-bed room, but it was listed for two people only.
* We booked it for two guests and paid an additional 400 EGP in cash for the third person, as the included breakfast was only for two.
* The staff let us choose between two available rooms, which was a nice touch.

Location – Perfect for Sightseeing
The hotel’s location is fantastic, especially if you're planning to explore Luxor’s iconic sites:
* A short walk to the Nile, where you can take a ferry to visit the Valley of the Kings, Valley of the Queens, and the Temple of Hatshepsut.
* Close to the Avenue of the Sphinxes, which connects Karnak Temple to Luxor Temple.

Cleanliness Issues
Unfortunately, the cleanliness did not meet expectations:
* One of our friends found clipped nails on his bed and requested a sheet change.
* Due to a miscommunication, instead of just changing the sheets, the staff replaced the entire bed—which, while unnecessary, was appreciated.

Breakfast & Dining
The included breakfast was great, featuring:
* Tomatoes, peppers, Egyptian pita bread, two types of cream cheese, jam, and a beverage of choice.

Excellent Customer Service – Special Thanks to Ayman
On our check-out day, we were traveling to Aswan, but we wanted to stop at Edfu and Kom Ombo temples along the way.
* The hotel manager, Ayman, arranged a private car for us to Aswan with stops at both temples.
* The entire full-day trip cost 90 USD—a fair price considering the long drive and stops.
* Ayman ensured everything was in order and was extremely helpful throughout.

A Thoughtful Gesture
Since we had to leave at 5 AM, we would miss breakfast, but the hotel prepared packed breakfasts for each of us. This small but thoughtful touch left a positive impression. (Photo attached!)

Final Thoughts
Windsor Hotel Luxor excels in service, location, and hospitality, but cleanliness needs improvement. If they address these issues, this would be a top-tier stay in Luxor.
Would I stay here again? Yes, but I’d check the room’s cleanliness first.

Definitely a great experience!  Although there is always a safety concern I felt very safe throughout the experience. The locals in charged of the hot air ballon flight as well as the pilot of the ballon did a great job. The tour was organized through Viking, the cruise line we took. It is not a cheap adventure but it is worth it! Flying over the Valley of the Kings was an incredible experience! To visit Luxor and the tombs on the Valley of The kings is a dream but seeing it from the the air was indescribable. We left the ship very early to be ready to take off by 6:30 am. From the ship we took a short bus drive and then we went across the Nile with a little cute ship. These hot air balloons carry up to 24 people each, but you don’t feel crowded as there is some room to move to take pictures. As the ballon starts lifting in the air and the sun appears in the horizon and you float over the Valley of the Kings, passing crop fields houses and monuments you are transported to another time, another era. It was incredible.  The ballon slowly spins and you get a 360 view through out your ride. The flight takes approximately 30 minutes, enough to see everything you want to see and experience. The landing was very professional and soft. After you disembark the basket you are offered the opportunity to buy a video on an USB. You also get a certificate from them to say you had a ballon ride. The ride back to the ship was quiet and peaceful as everyone was enjoying the experience we just had. Absolutely worth it. Really beautiful.

Wow, what an experience!  Now, ask me, like most people do 'if it's safe'.  This completely depends on your definition of safe.  By now, you've been driven around the country and have a rough idea of what that's like... so ballooning in

I think this was my favourite experience ever! To visit Egypt was a life long dream but never in a million  years did i expect to be seeing it from the angles I did in a Hot air ballon.

The experience was meant to take place once Saturday and then Sunday but due to weather conditions was put off until Monday morning, with a 4.20 pick up at the hotel. It was worth the 3.30 alarm clock on our last day.

We were taken to the dock at Luxor by minibus transfer, before hoping on a boat that took us across the river with coffee and a twinky. Then once across you hop into another minibus the other side to take you to the Hot air ballon site.
As you drive into the compound, you can't help but feel excited at the shear sight of these amazing Air ballons being set up.
It's not long before you are ready to climb into the 20+ passenger wicker basket with your Hot air ballon piolet and minutes after that, take off with a few blasts of fire/ hot air. You begin to take flight and leave all your troubles on the ground.

It was so beautiful getting to see other ballons take off at the same time and see these enormous spectacles take you up into the air.
We picked the first flight of the day to see the sun rise and boy was it worth the 10 pound difference.
You get to see the Tomb of Hapshetsut and float over the Valley, passing crop fields houses and great monuments. As the ballon rises and slowly spins you get a 360 view through out your ride.
The feeling you get is individual and so vast.
We had a group of Chinese tourists that broke out into song as the sun rose above the hills. Another woman cried tears of happiness and joy at the sites, another guy stuck firmly to the inside of the basket as he wa afraid of heights and I as well as being snap happy couldn't believe my lucky stars that I was getting to experience such beauty on a trip I'd only booked a few months earlier.

Once you have been up for 30 minutes or so you begin your decent into the desert area and make a soft landing where you are greeted by the landing team.
There are also a few locals who come asking for money, kids mainly.
After you disembark the basket you get a group photo with the captain and there is an opportunity to buy photos of the flight, video and USB.
We opted not to due to taking a butt load of pictures yourself.
You also get a certificate from them to say you had a ballon ride.
Then once your group is collected it's back to the river bank to make the trip to the other side of the river and back to your respective hotels.
We booked our trip through the tour rep at the hotel.

We booked a hot air balloon ride through Sun Pyramids Tours and were advised by their representative that they operated their own balloon company. After multiple price changes — despite being told the price was fixed — and only once we were about to board, it became clear that they were effectively brokering the ride rather than operating it.

Communication with Excellent hot air balloons was minimal beyond being provided with a pickup time. We were collected at 4:20am for a “sunrise” flight, then spent 90 minutes picking up other guests, followed by a boat crossing and another van ride. At the launch site, we waited another hour while more passengers were gathered. By the time our balloon launched, it was 30 minutes after sunrise. The basket was packed to capacity — 32 people with no room to maneuver — turning what should have been a serene experience into a gamble. Some balloons were still loading passengers over an hour after sunrise, entirely defeating the purpose of a sunrise flight.

The basket layout limits views, and although rotation was promised, it didn’t happen. The flight was noisy and chaotic, with the pilot’s radio blaring throughout. The return was equally disorganized, with no instructions and staff disappearing to arrange transport.
This experience failed to deliver on its core promise. Given that this is often an anticipated highlight, it's worth looking elsewhere. Not recommended.

​If you are debating whether a 4:00 AM alarm is worth it to float in a giant wicker basket over ancient history, stop thinking and just book it. Skyline Balloons runs a masterclass in logistics.
​When you first arrive at the launch site in the pre-dawn dark, it looks like beautiful, chaotic theater—dozens of massive balloons swallowing fire and inflating all around you. But don't be fooled; the ground crew operates like a high-stakes pit crew. It is incredibly efficient, safe, and perfectly timed.
​The takeoff itself was so unbelievably smooth that I didn't even realize we had left the earth until I looked down. Once you're aloft, the experience alternates between the powerful roar of the burner and a deep, surreal silence that you can't find anywhere else.
​Floating over the West Bank as the sun hits the desert is unmatched. You get a literal front-row seat to history: the dramatic cliffs, the Hatshepsut Temple, the Colossi of Memnon, and the stark contrast where the green Nile farmland slams right into the yellow desert sand. The pilot was fantastic—flawlessly spinning the balloon 360 degrees so every single corner of the basket got perfect photo angles, all while dropping great commentary and keeping the mood light.
​Smooth flight, expert landing, and memories that will stick around forever. If you’re coming to Luxor, this isn’t just a highlight; it’s the highlight. Massive props to the captain and the entire ground crew!

His art and passion for carving slate and limestone — depicting scenes from tombs and Egypt’s sacred places — result in creations worthy of the great pyramid builders.
He is likely the last truly traditional sculptor still practicing in Egypt today.

Each piece he creates is unique, crafted with rare skill, and carries the soul of the Valley of the Nobles. Bringing one of his works home means taking a living piece of Egypt with you, while also helping him continue his work among the tombs.

See you again soon, my dear friend, for another beautiful moment shared in your company.

I’m a female solo traveler, and I joined a two-day trip in Luxor with Skyscape.

First, I’d like to thank the Skyscape team. As a female solo traveler visiting Egypt for the first time, I truly appreciated the safe, prompt, and efficient communication provided before my trip.

Second, I want to give a big round of applause to my tour guide, Nour. She is incredibly detail-oriented, energetic, kind, and honest. (No awkward or forced jokes—just good vibes! 🤣) We spent two full days together, and she felt more like an old friend from back home than a guide. She clearly answered all my questions about history, and we had many fun and engaging conversations. I truly enjoyed having Nour as my guide—she made me feel safe and at ease throughout the trip. I was lucky to have a VIP tour with her as my companion.

Third, I joined the sunset felucca ride on the Nile River, which was such a wonderful experience. Thanks to the Skyscape team for arranging a fantastic crew, including a friendly captain, cheerful sailors, and Nour’s company. Plus, it was a private boat trip—I had the entire boat to myself! We danced, sang, and took amazing photos. I absolutely loved it and will definitely bring friends to join this tour again.

The only downside of the trip was the souvenir factory tour. The product prices were extremely high, and they refused to share the prices in advance. I felt pressured by the salespeople and ended up buying some items that I now regret purchasing 😭. If you book this tour, I recommend either skipping the factory stop or notifying Skyscape in advance that you don’t wish to include it.

Overall, I am still very happy with my two-day tour with Skyscape and Nour. If you’re looking for a VIP experience, don’t hesitate to contact them—and definitely ask for Nour as your guide!

Horses and Hieroglyphs. What an amazing vacation. We started in Cairo with Annmarie’s handpicked guides, touring the pyramids and local sites. The guide to Giza was a hoot. He took it upon himself to curate the funniest and most cinematic photoshoot I’ve ever had. Not to mention, because of his insider connections, you are given “unadvertised” privileges and exploration opportunities while on site. He went to great lengths to make sure our experience on the horses was safe, fun, and memorable. When we arrived in Luxor, we were taken straight to the operational headquarters, so to speak. On site villas where we would be spending our downtime, just a short walk from the stables. Beautifully furnished, spacious comfortable, and within direct access of the town if you desired to do any independent exploration. Whenever we were not eating in town, we would be eating poolside on the patio in this vicinity. The food… oh the food. I have literally never had better. EVERY SINGLE MEAL was so well seasoned and delicious. The best thing on the menu? The eggs. I know that sounds weird, but you don’t even know. To preface, I have had Gordon Ramsay’s eggs at the Hell’s Kitchen in Miami. Chef Adam’s eggs were better. This man’s food was so good, I purposed marriage. From what I understand, he’s currently unavailable. But, Adam, if you are out there, the offer still stands. Onto the stables: The riding excursions take you through the heart of the city to the outskirts of town. You get to experience every walk of life and interact directly with the community. It lends to intimate knowledge of the people and the land, if you are into the authentic experience and appreciate experiencing a place’s true culture, this is the trip for you. Fully enmeshed but fully safe and supported. The scenery is beautiful and the terrain varied so you are able to experience a wide variety of paces. Onto the horses: arguably the most important part. The horses have all been personally rescued and rehabilitated by the owners. The state these poor creatures were found in was truly deplorable and to see the level of recovery, health, and strength that they have been able to achieve is a testament to the deep love and devotion of Annmarie and Ganun to this cause. Not to mention the level of training. These horses are seriously well-trained and enjoyable to ride. And fast… did I mention they are FAST! Because all proceeds from the vacation package go directly to operating the organization of rehabilitation, this trip is one you can enjoy but also feel good about taking. This is a trip I fully intend to make a regular staple of my travel regimen. As a solo female traveler, I felt safe and still was able to experience adventure. This place, these people, couldn’t be more beautiful. They are now a part of my family and I’m grateful for the experience. I will definitely be coming back.

We took a taxi from Hugada to Luxor. It was less than a 5-minute drive from the hotel. Along the way, we saw nothing but desert and rocky mountains. I asked the driver if it rained, and he said it did, for about 5 minutes a year. There were no houses, no rest stops, and not much traffic. From my assessment, renting a car and driving between cities in Egypt wasn't ideal. We weren't familiar with the laws, road regulations, or the lack of amenities, even gas stations on the highway. As we entered the city, it became more humid, and we started to see trees. It took about 3 hours to reach Luxor. The city is fertile because the Nile River flows through it, so it's never dry. The city itself resembles India; the buildings look old, not very clean, and somewhat disorganized, unlike the five-star hotels we'd just seen. As the ancient capital of Egypt, Luxor has many ancient religious sites and tombs. We started our day in Luxor by waking up at 4 am and taking a boat across the Nile River to catch a hot air balloon tour to watch the sunrise and see the valley where the tombs of Tutankhamun and other kings of the Ramasate dynasty are located. With its long-standing legends, you can also see ancient temples, numerous cemeteries, and sugarcane fields stretching as far as the eye can see. It was an unforgettable hot air balloon ride experience, as the view before my eyes was the most beautiful I've ever seen.

My 4½-hour tour in Luxor was nothing short of extraordinary, and it was entirely thanks to my outstanding guide. From the very first moment we met, his punctuality and professionalism set the tone for a seamless and enriching experience. His communication was clear, thoughtful, and perfectly paced—never overwhelming, yet always deeply informative.
Our journey through the Valley of the Kings was unforgettable. Standing among the tombs of Egypt’s most powerful pharaohs is awe-inspiring on its own, but having a guide with such profound knowledge of ancient Egyptian history and dynasties elevated the experience to another level. He didn’t simply recite dates or names—he brought the New Kingdom to life. As we explored the intricate tomb chambers, he explained the symbolism in the wall carvings, the religious beliefs surrounding the afterlife, and the fascinating political shifts between dynasties. His passion for the subject was contagious.
At the magnificent Temple of Queen Hatshepsut, he skillfully told the story of one of Egypt’s most remarkable rulers. His explanation of how Hatshepsut established her legitimacy and reshaped her image in stone gave the temple’s grand terraces even deeper meaning. I walked away with a true appreciation for her legacy, something I would have completely missed without his insight.
Finally, at the Colossi of Memnon, he provided rich historical context while also knowing exactly where to stand for the best photographs. Throughout the tour, he effortlessly balanced scholarship with practicality—guiding me to ideal vantage points, avoiding crowds when possible, and ensuring I captured stunning photos to remember the day.
What truly distinguished him was the combination of expertise, enthusiasm, and genuine care for my experience. He was attentive, organized, and clearly dedicated to sharing Egypt’s history with authenticity and pride. I left Luxor not only with beautiful photos, but with a far deeper understanding of ancient Egypt. I cannot recommend him highly enough to anyone seeking an unforgettable and expertly guided journey through Luxor’s treasures.

The Abu Haggag Mosque is an active, historically significant mosque located directly inside the court of Ramesses II within the ancient Luxor Temple complex in Luxor, Egypt. The early foundation of the mosque dates back to 640 AD following the Arab conquest of Egypt. However, the formal structure seen today was constructed in the 13th century during the reign of the Ayyubid sultan As-Salih Ayyub. The mosque honors and houses the tomb of Sheikh Yusuf Abu al-Haggag, a prominent Sufi scholar born in Baghdad.

An older man approached us near the East Bank and offered a boat ride to the West Bank for 100 EGP. It sounded reasonable, so we agreed. Once we were on the way, he started persuading us to stop at his cafe/restaurant for food. Despite our hesitation, he kept insisting until we agreed to sit down.

We calmly said that without a menu we cannot order food and asked to leave. At this point, the man completely lost his temper. He started shouting, arguing, and abusing us, trying to intimidate us for refusing to order.

The place was filthy, unhygienic, and run by people who rely on tourist traps and pressure tactics. The cheap boat ride is just bait to force tourists into this restaurant and make them order without any price transparency.

This behaviour is unacceptable and unsafe for travellers. Avoid this place completely and do not trust anyone offering “cheap” rides who then pressures you into eating at their establishment.

Deir el-Bahari or Dayr al-Bahri (meaning Monastery of the North) is a complex of mortuary temples and tombs located on the west bank of the Nile, opposite the city of Luxor, Egypt. This is a part of the Theban Necropolis.

The first monument built at the site was the mortuary temple of Mentuhotep II of the Eleventh Dynasty. It was constructed during the 21st century BC.

During the Eighteenth Dynasty, Amenhotep I and Hatshepsut also built extensively at the site.

IN THE SHADOW OF THE CLIFFS - HATSHEPSUT'S TIMELESS MONUMENT

We visited the Temple of Hatshepsut on a weekday morning in the last week of January 2026, soon after our exploration of the Valley of the Kings. The setting was striking—an austere, desert landscape that strongly reminded us of Ladakh, with barren hills, stark cliffs, and not a trace of greenery in sight.

The monument itself is both elegant and meaningful. Built in memory of a queen who ruled as pharaoh, the temple stands as a powerful statement of authority and legacy. Its three terraces are thoughtfully laid out, and we spent nearly two hours moving through them, absorbing the reliefs, columns, and expansive views of the surrounding desert.

One practical aspect visitors should keep in mind is the exposure to the sun. There is very little shade while approaching the temple, and the open forecourt can be quite harsh, even in winter months. Carrying water, head protection, and planning the visit early in the day can make a significant difference.

Despite the heat and stark terrain, the experience is memorable. The combination of dramatic landscape, architectural symmetry, and the historical significance of a woman pharaoh makes the visit both reflective and rewarding. It remains one of Luxor’s most distinctive and thought-provoking sites.
Polish-Egyptian archeological teams are working on bringing some glory to this temple, and as it is a big one it would require time and effort, but it could be well worth the wait.

Title: A Journey Through Time: Exploring the Enchanting East and West Bank of Luxor with Get Luxor Tours

Introduction:
Embarking on a voyage to Luxor, Egypt, is like stepping into a time machine that transports you to the heart of ancient civilization. Nestled along the banks of the majestic River Nile, Luxor is a treasure trove of historical wonders. Get Luxor Tours, a renowned travel company, offers an unforgettable experience by guiding visitors through the captivating East and West Bank, unraveling the secrets of this mesmerizing destination. Join us on a creative review as we delve into the unique journey they provide.

East Bank:
The East Bank of Luxor is a vibrant district that pulsates with life and modernity. Get Luxor Tours ensures a seamless introduction to this bustling part of the city. Their expert guides paint a vivid picture of Luxor's present-day culture, all while paying homage to its magnificent past. Strolling along the lively streets, visitors are treated to a sensory feast of colors, sounds, and aromas.

As the sun sets, the East Bank transforms into a magical wonderland. The Luxor Temple, illuminated against the night sky, exudes an ethereal ambiance. Get Luxor Tours orchestrates a captivating visit to this iconic site, providing historical insights and allowing visitors to marvel at the temple's grandeur. The experience is nothing short of awe-inspiring, as the ancient stones whisper tales of pharaohs and gods.

West Bank:
Crossing over to the West Bank of Luxor, travelers are transported to an archaeological paradise. Get Luxor Tours expertly navigates the rich tapestry of this region, where ancient tombs and temples stand as testaments to the grandeur of the past. The Valley of the Kings, home to the final resting places of pharaohs, is a highlight of the journey. The guides from Get Luxor Tours bring history to life, regaling visitors with stories of legendary rulers and the intricate beliefs of the afterlife.

The enchanting mortuary temple of Hatshepsut, rising majestically against the backdrop of the desert, is another gem awaiting exploration. Get Luxor Tours unveils the captivating narrative of Egypt's first female pharaoh, revealing her remarkable achievements and the symbolism woven into the temple's structure.

A journey to the West Bank would be incomplete without a visit to the Colossi of Memnon. These towering statues of Amenhotep III guard the entrance to the Theban Necropolis, silently witnessing the passage of time. Get Luxor Tours provides an opportunity to appreciate these colossal guardians up close and personal, allowing visitors to connect with the profound history they represent.

Conclusion:
Get Luxor Tours offers a captivating journey through time, leading visitors on an immersive exploration of Luxor's East and West Bank. Their knowledgeable guides provide an invaluable understanding of the rich heritage and ancient wonders that make this destination truly extraordinary. Whether wandering through the bustling streets of the East Bank or delving into the archaeological treasures of the West Bank, Get Luxor Tours ensures an unforgettable experience that will leave you with a deep appreciation for Luxor's timeless allure.

Islam , a worker at the hotel , is kind and helpful. The prices he says are the real price. I paid him for the airport pickup and boats in a mixture of USD and EGP.

The pictures are 100 %  accurate, Luxor is very hot so the AC in the bedroom is great and the fan in the living room is good. The balcony and rooftop are beautiful but honestly it's so hot in Luxor you won't use them unless you're a camel or maybe Winter time here is better.

The kitchen is nice for drinks and snacks but no cooking is allowed as a safety rule. I didn't know that but the hotel politely explained it and I accepted it with no issues.

The airport or train station pickup is 20usd which depending on how many bags or how tired you are is worth it.

The hotel has a connection with a local boat guy named Ramadhan it's only 30egp or 1 dollar to cross 1 way(whole boat not per person) they're very quick and good at pick up, just add their what's app.

There is no Uber or Careem or indriver in Luxor but the taxi are all very fair. Just name a price you're happy with and they'll accept 90 %  of the time.

The wifi will be good enough for 95 %  of the people, I had to work via video call and it was good not great. But for youtube or FB it's fine.

The space itself is so nice, big western sofa. Big dining table, good kitchenette, giant wardrobe in the bedroom, mirror, lots of electric outlets[some hotels in Egypt have just 1 or 2] bed side tables are nice,

Tuktuk to the town area is 20 egp or about 65cents just name your price before you get in. It's a 15 minute walk to the West Bank downtown I PREFER west Bank over east Bank, this hotel is on West side.

EL HUSSEIN restaurant is great for breakfast lunch and dinner  100 %  local prices, good meats and breads.

The bathroom has a nice bidet , if you haven't tried bidet before give it a shot. There's also toilet paper.

And honestly you don't need to do Luxor AND Karnak just pick 1.

Ps. Hamada market is 2 minutes walk away and have local prices. They've got oatmeal, milk, cola, sweets, everything you need for holiday here

Pss. I HATE noise and there was no noise here at night I didn't even need my earplugs.

Helpful Hints:
•	Going inside the Great Pyramid involves climbing in a tight, steep, and very hot passageway — you’ll need to bend and climb narrow stairs or ladders.

•	Bring a hat, sunglasses, sunscreen, and some Egyptian pounds if you plan to shop or tip along the way.

We were recently on a tour of Egypt and had decided to arrive early to settle in with lthe local time zone. We were looking for a few low key things to do to start our Egyptian experiences.

Day 1
Met up with Mustafa , Medhut & Mohammad at 11am for our GEM excursion to be followed up by dinner on the Nile in a small boat. Once again, crazy driving in Cairo streets on way to GEM, but Mohammad safely got us there. First sight was pyramids was amazing, rising up over the city scape. Lots of construction still at the GEM. Security check points where the guards circled the van with a mirror looking under the van for potential issues. The size of the GEM is decieving but simply massive. The 40 foot statue of Ramses II is dwarfed by the immense scale of the lobby. Many were taking pictures or having their pictures taken in front of him. I managed to mistep and almost fell into the pool of water surrounding him. Scared my husband and the guides who now proceded to warn me of steps.... 12 galleries full of statues, sarcophagi, tools, items of daily living and more. We were guided by Medhut to see highlights which took almost 3 hours. We had some free time to grab a small bite at Starbucks & to charge our phones before heading back to Giza for our next excursion. BUT first had to shop in the museum gift shop for a beautiful scarf. Prices were reasonable. Then off to Cafelucca for private dinner on boat with Medhut who explained the Mediterranean foods to us. He has had an interesting professional history. We were then entertained by our waiting who sang and played the tambourine. Jim tried it also.

Day 2
Our excursions today were to head to Saqqara to see Tomb of Horemheb and the Serapeum. We met up with Mustafa & Medhut who had a new driver (forgot his name, something with an A, perhaps Ahmed). We arrived to Saqqara in a hour and headed off towards Tomb of Horemheb. We were treated to a surprise entry to Tomb of Maya. Great friezes on the walls. Tomb is rarely opened, so there was a musty odor. It was well preserved considering it's age. Then we went to Tomb of Horemheb which was next door. It had been pillaged in the past and many statues, stellas & friezes were missing. The pillars were mostly intact. Many great scenes of prisoners, of Horemheb & his wife and the gods. Quick ride to Serapeum, right pass the Step Pyramid of Djoser and the collapsed Pyramid. We declined pictures with camels, rides on camels and buying of scarves. The saracophigi were massive and very impressive. How did they get them down to the tunnels and niches??? Lunch at Tasty House was buffet style. Great selection. Hate to say it was the best meal we had so far. Dropped back off at hotel where we said our goodbyes to Mustafa and Medhut. Back to room to rest before looking for dinner. Early night as we meet up with our tour group at 830a to start our travels

Unforgettable Experience with Adam – Couldn’t Recommend Him More

We spent four of our seven days in Luxor and the surrounding areas with Adam as our guide, and those four days ended up being the absolute highlight of our trip. From start to finish, Adam was friendly, polite, always on time, and full of fascinating knowledge about Egypt’s incredible history. He made everything feel easy and personal, and we genuinely enjoyed every moment with him.

Day 1 started with visits to the Luxor Museum, the Mummification Museum, and the local souk. Adam’s knowledge of ancient Egypt, especially the 18th to 20th dynasties, really brought everything to life. You could tell how passionate he is, and he explained things in such an engaging and clear way. It was a brilliant introduction to what was to come.

Day 2 took us to the Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut’s Temple, the Tombs of the Nobles, and the Colossi of Memnon. This was one of our most memorable days—walking through the tombs while Adam told us the stories behind each one was fascinating. He answered every question we threw at him with ease and depth, and made what could have been just another sightseeing day into something really special.

Day 3 was spent exploring Luxor and Karnak Temples, and again Adam’s knowledge and storytelling made all the difference. He pointed out details in the carvings we never would have noticed ourselves and explained which kings and queens were behind each part of the temple complexes. We also visited a papyrus workshop where we learnt how it’s made, which was both fun and informative.

That night we had an incredible Bedouin camp experience in the desert, behind the Valley of the Kings. It was so peaceful, away from the noise of the city, with a delicious dinner and even a few desert foxes making an appearance. The next morning, we were up early to race across the desert to a stunning viewpoint and watch the sunrise. Seeing the hot air balloons rise on the horizon as the sun came up was absolutely magical—one of those moments you’ll never forget.

Day 4 was a day trip to Dendera Temple, and what a beautiful place it was. As with everywhere else we visited, Adam’s knowledge really brought the site to life and gave us a real appreciation for the art and architecture.

What really stood out throughout was Adam himself—he’s not just a brilliant guide, but a genuinely lovely person. Warm, respectful, funny, and incredibly well-informed. It felt like we were travelling with a friend who happened to know everything there is to know about ancient Egypt.

If you’re planning a visit to Luxor, we honestly can’t recommend Adam enough. He made our trip unforgettable.

The Silk Road restaurant at the Hilton Luxor Resort & Spa is easily one of the standout dining experiences in Luxor. Set against the serene backdrop of the Nile, the restaurant blends a relaxed, elegant atmosphere with a menu that takes you on a journey across Asian and Middle Eastern flavours.

From the moment you arrive, the service from the Waiter Redwan feels attentive without being overbearing, and the setting, especially in the evening, is calm and beautifully lit. The food itself is where Silk Road truly shines. Each dish is thoughtfully presented, with a clear focus on freshness and balance of flavours.

A special mention has to go to Chef Amira, who did an amazing job. Her attention to detail and passion for the cuisine really comes through in every dish. You can tell there’s a personal touch in the way the food is prepared and presented, elevating the entire dining experience.

Overall, Silk Road is a must-visit if you’re staying at or near the Hilton Luxor Resort & Spa. It offers not just great food, but a memorable dining experience that combines atmosphere, service, and genuine culinary talent.

Just finished our ride. Hopefully this will help others with their planning:

There are 2 flight times. Sunrise (first ride) and after sunrise (second ride). There are about 24 companies. Sunrise is about 50% more expensive. We did the sunrise ride. We saw prices of 65 USD or around 6000egp. The first 2 companies were full for sunrise. Third had availability. So if they tell you full, keep trying.

We flew with BEYOND HORIZON. We paid 7000 total. 2k cash to the driver that booked it for us. 5k directly to the balloon company. The company accepted credit cards (great!), but they added 3% extra for it.

Hotel pick up times varied from 4:30 to 5:30am. The closer your hotel is to the West Bank bridge, the later your pickup time.

When you get to the take off point on the west bank, the balloons fly in 2 groups. Each company runs 2 balloons that depart about 15 minutes after each other. First balloon launches before sunrise. Our balloon was second and launched a few minutes after sunrise.

My expectation was the balloons would fly close to the temples over the desert. SOME did. A few flew very low over the ruins hovering over temples. Those looked amazing.

Other balloons (like ours) drifted towards the Nile and over the green fields. I don't know how much control the companies have over their flight path. But they clearly do have some control about how they move.

We were told total flight time would be 35 minutes. Our ride was about 20. We were in the second batch to take off and one of the first to land again. Landing happened in a farmer's field so you have to walk through his seedling crops to get to the road. Wear appropriate shoes. The same van met us there and drove us back.

Beyond Horizon took photos and recorded videos. I'm not sure if all the companies do that. After the flight you can purchase the photos and video for an additional 800.

Overall it's a great experience, but if I do it again I would choose a different company. I don't know if other companies have permission to fly closer to the temples. If so I would choose one of those. It also seems better to be on the FIRST balloon in the sunrise group.
We had an amaizing experience, and are grateful to the skilled commander for the smooth flight and excellent landing.

I spent four nights in Luxor, and every single night I had dinner at Baladi. That alone should say something.
The first night was pure accident. I was walking past, had gone slightly further down the street, and everything else around felt overtly touristy. Baladi stood out immediately: authentic, calm, beautifully appointed, and quietly confident. I walked in without expectations, and within minutes realised I had stumbled upon something extraordinary.
The food is, quite simply, unbelievable. From the very first meal, it was clear this was not just “good local food”; it was food cooked with pride, generosity, and deep understanding. After that first night, there was no question of eating anywhere else. I returned the next three nights without hesitation.
The menu is refreshingly simple in concept but vast in choice. There is a huge selection of main dishes, all priced at 400 EGP, and that price is almost laughable given what you receive. Each main dish comes with an astonishing spread: enormous portions of perfectly cooked rice, fresh baladi bread, vegetables, multiple sauces, salads, and accompaniments, and then more of all of that. You do not need to ask for extra servings. They just arrive. And if you hesitate, they insist you eat more.
The generosity is not performative; it is genuine. The courtesy, kindness, and hospitality shown here are on another level altogether. You are not treated like a customer; you are treated like a guest, almost like family. It genuinely felt like they were looking after us, night after night, with warmth and sincerity that is increasingly rare anywhere in the world.
The atmosphere deserves special mention. Baladi is spacious, immaculately clean, extremely tidy, and very well appointed. The entire area has a quiet, subdued feel, which makes dining here deeply comfortable and relaxed. There is no noise, no rush, no pressure, just calm, space, and exceptional food. It feels refined without being pretentious, traditional without being dated.
As for the food itself, it is incomparable. After four nights of eating here, I genuinely doubt I will be able to go back home and get used to “regular” food again. Every dish is deeply satisfying, balanced, and memorable. This is food fit for kings, served with humility and grace.
To be clear, the 400 EGP price point is a pittance. Once you factor in the sheer volume and quality of the rice, bread, vegetables, salads, sauces, and repeated refills, it borders on absurd value. You leave full, content, and slightly in disbelief.
The hospitality is something I will remember for a lifetime. The food is more than first class. The atmosphere is first class. Everything about Baladi reflects care, pride, and generosity.
To any prospective guest: you would be an idiot to skip this place and eat elsewhere. If you are in Luxor and you miss Baladi, you have genuinely missed one of the best experiences the city has to offer.
Baladi is not just a restaurant. It is an experience, and one I feel incredibly fortunate to have found.

DRIFTING THROUGH TIME - A JANUARYI VOYAGE ON THE NILE

Cruising the Nile from Aswan to Luxor is less a journey and more a graceful immersion into history, geography, and rhythm of the ancient civilisation of Egypt. Our three-day cruise in January—arguably the most pleasant season—combined comfortable weather with luminous skies and calm waters, making the experience both relaxed, enriched and reflective.

Beginning at Aswan and ending at Luxor, the voyage unfolded at an unhurried pace. One of the early highlights was the stop at Edfu, where the proximity of the temple to the river reinforces how deeply the Nile shaped ancient Egyptian life. Equally memorable was crossing the Esna Locks, which in fact is a barrage. What might seem a routine engineering operation turned into a fascinating lesson in river management, navigation, and coordination. Watching multiple vessels queue, negotiate water levels, and pass through in sequence was both entertaining and educational.

Traveling as a large group added a lively social dimension. Conversations flowed easily on deck as the scenery slipped by—lush green banks, date palms, villages, and the occasional felucca. A striking observation was how most cruise ships operate on a synchronized schedule. Many vessels start sailing around the same time, which means actual sailing hours are relatively short compared to the time spent anchored. Yet, this never felt like a drawback. On the contrary, the long anchored periods allowed for excursions, rest, and quiet contemplation of the river.

Life onboard followed a gentle routine: mornings opening to misty vistas, afternoons spent watching the Nile glide past, and evenings marked by soft lights reflecting on water. January’s mild temperatures made deck time especially enjoyable, without the fatigue that harsher months might bring.

Overall, the Nile cruise offered a rare blend of leisure and learning. It was serene without being idle, structured yet unhurried—an experience that lingers long after the river bends fade from view.

It was a dream of ours to have the opportunity to visit the wonders of Egypt, and it made it all more memorable with the lovely crew on board.
We boarded in Aswan, on a very hot day, which ended up being a little overwhelming for two Canadian travellers. The crew allowed us to board earlier than scheduled, and immediately cared for my father who was suffering from mild heat stroke, crafting a homemade mint drink to help cool him off and giving him a comfortable place to rest. I also found myself not feeling very well, and was treated to freshly brewed ginger tea to help ease my stomach. What could have been the start of a challenging journey was quickly turned around and revived by this thoughtful and caring crew.
The days we spent on board slowly travelling up the Nile from Aswan to Luxor, taking the sights along the way were idyllic, the accommodations were spotless and comfortable, and the food was delicious!
The itinerary was well crafted, providing us with enough time to explore without being rushed or feeling as though we missed any key sites.
Luxor is remarkable. The temples of Luxor, Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, the museums…too much to list! Visiting these sites with Farah Nile Cruise as our ‘home base’ provided the perfect backdrop to a trip of a lifetime for my father and I.
We have so much gratitude to the crew for contributing to our memories.

True Gentelman, very professional who dearly  loves Egypt, Luxor and  Egyptology .  Mr Moatty was know and respected by all the tour guides.  He has a big hart and helps all those who needs help. We spent 3 days and 4 nights on the Dahabiya Hathor, traveling from Aswan to Luxor, and overall it was a truly unforgettable experience.

The ship itself is beautiful — very modern and brand new. Since this was only the third trip the Dahabiya had ever done, there are still a few things that need improvement and fine-tuning. However, the entire crew was incredibly helpful and did everything they could to make our stay enjoyable.

We were actually the only guests on board during the cruise, which made the experience feel even more unique and personal. The crew adjusted the itinerary according to our wishes and needs, which we appreciated greatly.

One of the absolute highlights was a spontaneous stop at the Nile riverbank so we could swim in the Nile. The crew set up beach chairs for us right by the water and even brought us drinks while we were swimming. It was such a special and unforgettable moment that we will always remember.

The food on board was also excellent — delicious and very generous in portion size, although for us it was almost too much food at times. But perhaps that is simply part of the local hospitality and culture.

As the ship is still very new, there are a few technical aspects that could be improved, such as the hot water system, water filtration, jacuzzi water quality, and the AC. We mentioned these points several times, and the crew was always responsive and eager to help. We are sure these are normal adjustments for a brand-new ship and that everything will improve with more experience and time.

Overall, we would like to sincerely thank the entire crew for this wonderful and unforgettable journey on the Dahabiya Hathor.
