Outstanding Food and the Best Dining Location in Luxor - an unforgettable sunset dining experience by the Nile River.

These photos perfectly capture why Abydos was my favorite dining experience during my stay in Egypt.

From the moment the food arrived, I knew I was in for something special. The presentation was beautiful, with colorful dishes spread across the table, showcasing a wonderful selection of Egyptian flavors.

The star of the meal was the mixed grill. The grilled meats were tender, juicy, and packed with flavor. Every piece was cooked perfectly. The combination of grilled kebabs, meat cuts, and chicken made for a satisfying and memorable meal. Served alongside freshly baked pita bread, grilled vegetables, and delicious dips, it was a complete feast.

The lentil soup was rich, comforting, and full of flavor. The hummus and other traditional dips were smooth, fresh, and complemented the grilled meats perfectly. One of my favorite appetizers was the cheese spring rolls, which were crispy on the outside and wonderfully cheesy on the inside. The meat-filled pastries were equally delicious.

The fresh salads added a refreshing balance to the meal, It seems to be prepared using high-quality ingredients. What impressed me most was the consistency—every item on the table was genuinely enjoyable.

Beyond the food, the location makes Abydos truly special. Situated right on the banks of the Nile River, it offers one of the most beautiful dining settings in Luxor. Watching the sunset over the Nile while enjoying such an incredible meal created an unforgettable experience. The combination of stunning river views, a relaxing atmosphere, attentive service, and exceptional food made this dinner one of the highlights of my entire trip to Egypt.

The service deserves special recognition as well. The staff were attentive, friendly, and always ready to help without being intrusive. They made sure everything was perfect throughout the meal and were happy to answer questions and provide recommendations.

I would also like to thank the owner, Marco, who was incredibly kind and welcoming. It is clear that they take great pride in both the restaurant and the guest experience. Their warm personality and personal attention made us feel valued and added a special touch to an already wonderful evening.

Having visited several restaurants throughout Egypt, including popular spots in Cairo and around Khan El Khalili, I can confidently say that Abydos delivered the best overall dining experience of my trip. The food was fresher, more flavorful, and far more memorable than many of the places I tried during my stay in Egypt.

If you're visiting Luxor, don't miss the opportunity to dine at Abydos. Come hungry, arrive before sunset, and prepare for an unforgettable meal by the Nile. Between the outstanding food, spectacular views, attentive staff, and welcoming owner, Abydos is a restaurant that truly deserves its excellent reputation.

A Bright, Expansive Tomb Celebrated for Its Vivid Colors and Astronomical Ceiling

KV2 is one of the most visually impressive tombs in the valley, known for its excellent preservation and vibrant decoration. Ramesses IV, determined to secure his place in eternity, expanded the tomb’s scale and filled it with richly colored scenes from the Book of the Dead, Book of Caverns, and Litany of Ra.

The highlight is the burial chamber’s astronomical ceiling — a deep blue sky filled with constellations, deities, and celestial boats. It is one of the finest examples of ancient Egyptian star maps, symbolizing the king’s journey through the heavens.

The tomb’s wide corridors, clear inscriptions, and luminous colors make KV2 one of the most accessible and rewarding tombs for understanding New Kingdom funerary theology. It is a masterpiece of Ramesside art, full of cosmic symbolism and royal ambition.

The Tomb of Ramses IV (KV2) is one of the most frequently visited monuments in the Valley of the Kings, owing to its location close to the entrance and its inclusion in the standard admission ticket. Ramses IV, the third pharaoh of the 20th

KV2, the tomb of Ramesses IV, is a large and well-decorated tomb in the Valley of the Kings. Its walls are adorned with vivid scenes from the Book of the Dead and other funerary texts, offering insight into New Kingdom beliefs about the afterlife. The chambers are spacious, and the artwork remains remarkably visible, making it a fascinating stop for those exploring Luxor’s royal necropolis. KV2 provides a quieter, less crowded experience compared to some of the more famous tombs, allowing for a more immersive visit.

Smaller in scale but rich in detail, its paintings depict daily life, religious rituals, and the journey to the afterlife. The colors remain vibrant. The space is tight, so larger groups may find it difficult to move around. A short but worthwhile visit.

The Tomb of Ramose (TT55) is a remarkable funerary monument in the Sheikh Abd el-Qurna necropolis on the West Bank near Luxor, Egypt. Ramose, a high vizier and mayor of Thebes, served under Pharaoh Amenhotep III and the early Akhenaten around 1360 BCE. It features a long entrance, a large pillared hall (originally 32), side rooms, and an undecorated burial chamber. It is crowded, with well-preserved reliefs and vibrant colors that illustrate the artistic evolution.

This tomb belonged to Grand Vizier and Mayor Ramose of Thebes (14th century BC). It contains some of the finest relief carvings in Thebes. Unfortunately, some of the later paintings, created under the Aten cult, have been destroyed. A guided tour is highly recommended
